primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Type II pneumocytes produce surfactant, which lowers alveolar surface tension, increases compliance, and helps prevent end-expiratory alveolar collapse.
vignette: A premature infant has respiratory distress syndrome due to deficient pulmonary surfactant.
lead: Which physical property of the alveolus is most directly altered?
distractors: Surface tension is decreased below normal
distractor_notes: Surfactant normally lowers surface tension, so deficiency raises it.
Alveolar radius remains relevant to collapsing pressure.
Pulmonary perfusion does not cease solely from surfactant deficiency.
Hemoglobin affinity is not the primary defect.
key_expl: Without surfactant, alveolar surface tension increases and promotes collapse.
objective: Explain the effect of surfactant deficiency on alveolar mechanics.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Interstitial fibrosis increases elastic stiffness of the lung, reducing compliance and increasing the work required to inflate the lungs.
vignette: A patient with advanced pulmonary fibrosis has a small change in lung volume despite a large increase in transpulmonary pressure.
distractor_notes: Fibrotic lungs are stiff and therefore less compliant.
The pressure-volume relationship is clearly altered.
Compliance cannot physiologically be infinite here.
Compliance is not negative.
key_expl: Compliance is ΔV/ΔP; stiff fibrotic lungs have a smaller volume change for a given pressure change.
objective: Relate pulmonary fibrosis to decreased compliance.
clues: large pressure needed for small volume change

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Higher temperature, higher CO2, lower pH, and increased 2,3-BPG reduce hemoglobin oxygen affinity and facilitate tissue unloading.
vignette: Exercising skeletal muscle becomes warmer, more acidic, and produces more CO2.
lead: How does the local hemoglobin-oxygen dissociation curve change?
correct: It shifts to the right, promoting oxygen unloading
distractors: It shifts left, increasing oxygen affinity
It shifts right and prevents oxygen unloading
distractor_notes: A left shift would impair oxygen unloading.
The Bohr effect specifically links lower pH and higher CO2 to reduced affinity.
The curve remains sigmoidal.
A right shift facilitates, rather than prevents, release.
key_expl: The Bohr effect and higher temperature shift the curve right and enhance oxygen delivery to active tissues.
objective: Predict oxygen-hemoglobin affinity changes during exercise.

distractor_notes: S pneumoniae more commonly causes typical lobar pneumonia without the characteristic water exposure and diarrhea-hyponatremia pattern.
Mycoplasma typically affects younger patients.
Pneumocystis occurs in severe immunosuppression.
Klebsiella may cause necrotizing pneumonia but lacks the classic hotel-water association.

A type III secretion system is not its defining virulence factor.
Acid-fast cell walls characterize mycobacteria.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: At low plasma concentrations, para-aminohippurate is filtered and strongly secreted, so nearly all PAH entering the kidney is excreted and its clearance approximates effective renal plasma flow.
vignette: A research study infuses low-dose para-aminohippurate.
lead: Which physiologic variable does PAH clearance approximate?
distractors: Renal blood flow without hematocrit correction exactly
distractor_notes: Inulin or creatinine clearance approximates GFR.
RPF, not total blood flow, is directly approximated; hematocrit is needed to derive renal blood flow.
Filtration fraction is GFR/RPF.
Urine osmolality is a concentrating measure.
key_expl: Near-complete renal extraction of PAH makes its clearance an estimate of effective renal plasma flow.
objective: Identify PAH clearance as a measure of effective renal plasma flow.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: The proximal tubule reabsorbs most filtered sodium and water, essentially all normal filtered glucose and amino acids, and most bicarbonate.
vignette: A toxin selectively damages proximal tubular epithelial cells.
lead: Which filtered substance is most likely to appear abnormally in urine despite normal plasma concentration?
distractors: Creatinine due to loss of filtration only
Red blood cells from glomerular rupture only
distractor_notes: Creatinine handling depends on filtration and secretion; proximal injury can affect secretion but glucosuria is a classic reabsorptive loss.
Albuminuria primarily reflects glomerular barrier defects.
RBCs in urine suggest glomerular or urinary tract bleeding.
Unconjugated bilirubin from hemolysis is not filtered.
key_expl: Normal filtered glucose is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule, so proximal dysfunction can cause normoglycemic glucosuria.
objective: Identify a proximal tubular reabsorptive function.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: The thick ascending limb reabsorbs NaCl through NKCC2 while remaining nearly impermeable to water, making tubular fluid more dilute.
vignette: Fluid enters the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.
lead: Which change normally occurs along this segment?
correct: Tubular fluid becomes more dilute as NaCl is reabsorbed without water
distractors: Tubular fluid becomes more concentrated because water leaves freely
Glucose is the primary solute reabsorbed here
distractor_notes: The thick ascending limb is water impermeable.
Glucose reabsorption occurs in proximal tubule.
Urea handling is more important in medullary collecting duct and thin limbs.
NKCC2 mediates substantial sodium transport.
key_expl: Salt removal without water makes the thick ascending limb a diluting segment.
objective: Explain why the thick ascending limb dilutes tubular fluid.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

distractors: Increased potassium reabsorption with sodium loss
Complete inhibition of hydrogen secretion in all nephron cells
distractor_notes: Aldosterone increases ENaC expression/activity.
It increases basolateral Na-K ATPase activity.
It promotes potassium secretion rather than retention in principal cells.
It can enhance acid secretion in intercalated cells rather than completely inhibit it.
key_expl: Aldosterone increases distal sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion.
objective: Predict aldosterone effects on collecting-duct principal cells.
